title: Runtime quant adapter contracts and KV coherence (draft)
content:
Status: draft — working notes for runtime/adapter/kernel/kv interactions

Purpose
- Capture a concrete, testable contract for the "quant adapter" layer that sits between the high-level scheduler and low-level kernel implementations, specifically for INT8, FP8, GPTQ, and AWQ execution paths.
- Surface constraints that schedulers, KV-cache, and rollout/rollback systems must respect.
- Outline fallback and coherence behaviors when mixing precision variants across batches or during runtime rollouts.

Background / motivation
We are increasingly supporting mixed-precision serving where: some requests execute on INT8 optimized kernels, others on FP8, and certain model checkpoints are shipped with GPTQ/AWQ quantized weights. The runtime must:
  - route requests to compatible kernel artifacts,
  - maintain KV cache coherency across precision boundaries,
  - guarantee graceful degradation when a kernel fails or is incompatible with cached state.

High-level design overview\- Quant Adapter role (brief):
  - Query capability: determine if a given model variant + sequence length + batch shape can be served by a specific kernel blob (artifact).
  - Transform metadata: translate scheduling decisions into kernel invocation parameters (bitwidth, scale table id, reorder flags).
  - Compatibility checks: decide whether KV cache entries are usable for an incoming request given the kernel and model quantization.
  - Fallback orchestration: signal scheduler and tracer which fallback path to take (route-to-fp32, route-to-different-kernel, or recompute without cache).

Compatibility matrix (informal)
Rows: source state (what produced the KV entries / previous tokens)
Cols: target kernel to execute the next tokens
Rules: "OK" means KV can be reused without transformation; "transformable" means adapter can cheaply convert; "incompatible" means KV must be invalidated and recomputed.

- FP32-origin KV -> FP32 kernel: OK
- FP32-origin KV -> FP8 kernel: transformable (requires scale table estimation; small quantization error tolerated)
- FP32-origin KV -> INT8 kernel: transformable with higher error; only allowed under explicit policy (latency-first)
- FP32-origin KV -> GPTQ/AWQ kernel: incompatible unless a deterministic conversion path exists (rare)

- FP8-origin KV -> FP8 kernel: OK
- FP8-origin KV -> INT8 kernel: transformable? generally NO unless precomputed down-quantization mapping exists
- FP8-origin KV -> GPTQ/AWQ kernel: incompatible

- INT8-origin KV -> INT8 kernel: OK
- INT8-origin KV -> FP8 kernel: transformable but quality-risk; prefer recompute for safety
- INT8-origin KV -> GPTQ/AWQ kernel: incompatible

- GPTQ/AWQ-origin KV -> GPTQ/AWQ kernel: OK if bit-packing/layout identical
- GPTQ/AWQ-origin KV -> any non-GPTQ kernel: incompatible (layout + scale semantics differ)

NOTE: above matrix encodes *conservative defaults*. Operational policy (in Redwood Console) can relax where acceptable. The quant adapter must provide deterministic rationale flags for each compatibility decision so that tracing, audits, and automated evals can reason about accuracy impact.

Kernel constraints per quant format\- INT8 kernels\  - Input layout: int8 NCHW-like intermediate packing (implementation-specific).\  - Requires: scale table id + zero point semantics for each attention matmul block.\  - Alignment: 32-byte alignment for SIMD kernels; batch shapes padded to multiples of 8 tokens in global batching.\  - KV format: packed int8 + header with scale_id and per-layer quant metadata.\  - Failure modes: overflow on accumulation (rare), scale mismatch -> catastrophic tokens.\- FP8 kernels\  - FP8 variant: E4M3 and E5M2 considered.\  - Requires: exponent bias table and stochastic clamp policy for residuals.\  - KV format: floating mantissa preserved; more tolerant to dynamic range but requires careful accumulation to avoid underflow.\  - Alignment: 16-byte preferred.\  - Failure modes: numerics drift over long contexts; recompute or apply dequant-delta correction.\- GPTQ/AWQ kernels\  - Packed weight layout (per-channel scales, bitpacking metadata).\  - Compatible only with identical bitpacking and permutation semantics.\  - KV format: typically FP16 or FP32 internal activations stored; kernels assume specific weight dequant path and cannot accept external INT8/FP8-packed KV.\  - Failure modes: mismatch leads to invalid attention keys/values -> coherence break.

Adapter API / ABI (proposal)\- Input to adapter: model_id, model_variant_tag (e.g., "gpt2-xl-awq-v2"), kernel_artifact_hash, request_shape {batch_size, seq_len, prefix_len}, kv_header (if present), scheduler_hint (latency/cost/quality preference).
- Output: decision {action: USE_KERNEL | TRANSFORM_KV | INVALIDATE_KV | RECOMPUTE_PREFIX, transformation_plan: string, reason_code: short_string, estimated_quality_delta: numeric-string}.

(Implementation note: keep the output fields string-typed for logging/tracing; runtime core will parse these.)

KV cache implications and coherence rules\- Cache keys must include quant metadata: model_variant, kernel_artifact_hash, bitwidth_tag, scale_table_id, and packing_layout_id.
- When a kernel is rolled out or a request is routed to a different quant path, the adapter can:
  1) reuse existing KV if compatible (fast path),
  2) apply on-the-fly transformation (cheap path) for allowed combinations, or
  3) mark entries stale and trigger prefix recompute (safe path).
- Transformations should be applied lazily and attached to request trace; the adapter must keep metrics on transformation cost and measured accuracy delta.

Scheduling impacts and constraints\- Batching: Quant kernels have different padding/alignment requirements. Scheduler must respect per-kernel token padding constraints to avoid OOM or incorrect results.\- Co-location: when packing heterogeneous requests into a batch, only group requests that share compatible kernel artifact and quant metadata. If mixed precision in a batch is unavoidable, prefer serial execution or split micro-batches per precision.\- Preheat / warm pools: maintain small warm pools for each quant artifact that preserve pre-computed JIT kernels and relevant scale tables. Warm pool size configurable per model variant.

Fallback policy (runtime behavior)\- Primary goal: keep tail-latency SLOs without unbounded quality regressions.
- On kernel failure or incompatibility:
  1) if policy=latency-first => route to compatible lower-precision kernel (if KV transformable) or to dedicated FP32 fallback instance (if available).\ 2) if policy=quality-first => invalidate KV and recompute prefix on safe kernel (FP32/FP16) possibly incurring latency.\ 3) if policy=safe-rollout => automatically revert traffic fraction to previous kernel artifact and tag traces for offline eval.
- All fallback actions must produce machine-readable reason_code and correlation_id for tracing.

Testing and validation plan\- Unit tests: compatibility decision table for all pairwise combinations of {FP32, FP16, FP8(E4M3/E5M2), INT8, GPTQ, AWQ}. Use synthetic KV headers to assert expected adapter outputs.
- Integration tests: end-to-end with KV cache enabled; inject mismatch headers and verify that user-visible tokens match baseline within configured quality thresholds.
- Perf tests: measure transformation cost (ms) and ensure it remains bounded under normal SLOs.
- A/B experiments: rollout quant kernels behind canary flag with traffic shaping and monitor quality regressions on a reserved prompt set.

Operational telemetry and tracing\- Emit (per request): adapter_decision, compatibility_reason, transformation_latency_ms, kv_reuse_flag, prior_kernel_hash, chosen_kernel_hash, policy_tag.
- Expose dashboards: %kv_reuse_by_kernel, transform_cost_histogram, fallback_rate_by_model, accuracy_regression_alerts (hook to Optimize).

Open questions / unresolved items\- Exact binary format for KV transforms: should we standardize a single on-wire transform format or keep per-adapter code?\- Transform precision knobs: do we expose a continuous confidence score for "estimated_quality_delta" or keep discrete buckets?\- Should scheduler be allowed to preemptively invalidate KV on model rollout to avoid partial-compatibility-induced drift?

Next steps (short term)\- Implement adapter interface stub in runtime core (ENG-1279).\- Add compatibility unit tests and a small synthetic GPTQ->FP8 conversion harness.\- Prototype lazy transform path for FP32->FP8 and measure cost/accuracy.

Notes to reviewers
- Be pragmatic: prefer conservative defaults for safety but design hooks to relax policies via Console.
- This doc intentionally leaves many implementation details open; aim to converge on an ABI and the compatibility matrix decisions in the next 2 sprints.

TODOs\- [ ] Define transform serialization format\- [ ] Add per-layer quant metadata to model manifest\- [ ] Add adapter metrics to tracing schema\- [ ] Schedule experimental rollout for awq-v2 on canary cluster

End of draft.
